questions.prompt: Why did the Linear B tablets survive?

options.text: They were hardened by a fire.

questions.explanation: 'a fire that destroyed the palace baked them hard'.

questions.prompt: What was the importance of Blegen's discovery at Pylos?

options.text: It proved the language was Greek.
It showed the script was used outside Crete.
It allowed Evans to publish his work.

questions.explanation: 'it showed the script was used beyond Crete'.

options.text: that the language changed word endings

questions.explanation: The language 'must be inflected, changing the endings of words'.

questions.prompt: How did Ventris make his breakthrough?

options.text: by comparing the script with Etruscan
by guessing sounds for likely place names
by asking Chadwick to translate the tablets
by using a newly found tablet from Pylos

questions.explanation: He used words he 'guessed might be place names on Crete'.
questions.trap: D — the Pylos tripod tablet CONFIRMED the decipherment in 1953.

groups.instructions: Match each statement with the correct person, A–E. You may use any letter more than once.

questions.prompt: worked mainly without help, outside normal working hours
questions.explanation: Kober worked 'largely alone, in her spare time'.

questions.prompt: delayed making material available to others
questions.explanation: Evans 'was also slow to publish the tablets in full'.

questions.prompt: verified that the language was an early form of Greek
questions.explanation: Chadwick 'confirmed that the language was indeed Greek'.

questions.prompt: first became interested in the script as a child
questions.explanation: Ventris had been fascinated 'since hearing Evans lecture when he was a schoolboy'.

questions.prompt: tested the decipherment on a new piece of evidence
questions.explanation: Blegen 'applied Ventris's values to a newly discovered tablet'.

questions.explanation: 'Ventris arranged the signs in a grid'.
